column38:
Recently, we witnessed a moment that reminded us just how powerful God’s love and mercy truly are. A young girl came to us carrying a heavy burden. For a long time, she had been struggling under the grip and confusion of witchcraft—something that had brought fear, turmoil, and darkness into her young life. You could see the weight in her eyes, the kind of weight no young person should ever have to carry.

As we walked with her, we were reminded of the words of our Lord Jesus Christ, when He told His disciples that “this kind can only come out by prayer and fasting.” So we did exactly that. We prayed. We fasted. We trusted God. Not because of our own strength, but because we knew that true deliverance comes from Him alone.

And then, by the grace and power of God, something beautiful happened. The chains that had held her captive were broken. The fear that once filled her heart gave way to peace. The darkness lifted, and in its place came freedom and hope. Watching her step into that freedom was a moment none of us will forget.

To us, this is not a story about what we did. It is a testimony of what God can do. Our greatest joy is simply to witness young people being set free—from fear, from bondage, from anything that seeks to destroy the destiny God has placed within them.

Last Sunday, I was invited to preach in one of the schools. The service began early in the morning, as is usually the case, with the audience consisting mainly of students and, occasionally, a patron or the teacher on duty. However, this particular Sunday was different, as the Christian Union patron was not present. I was instead received and ushered in by the student chairlady.
After I had concluded the ministry, a lady—whom I initially assumed to be a teacher—stood up to speak. She expressed her appreciation for the sermon and shared a personal testimony that greatly encouraged me.
She explained that this was not the first time she had listened to me preach. Her first encounter was in 2017 at the same school, when I spoke on the topic of sexual purity. After completing her final exams, she did not attain the grade she had hoped for and later transferred to another school to repeat. By God’s providence, I was also invited to speak at that school, again on the same topic.
She shared that hearing the message on sexual purity twice made a profound impact on her life. She took it as a confirmation from God and made a personal decision to walk in purity. Additionally, she committed herself to serving God through student ministry.
Today, she is working in the medical field at a hospital and is doing well professionally. She expressed great joy that Youth for Christ continues to consistently teach and uphold the message of sexual purity across generations. Even nine years later, she clearly remembers the teachings and has remained a strong advocate for purity. While others promote contraceptive use among teenagers, she actively encourages young people to pursue purity.
This testimony was deeply encouraging and served as a strong motivation for me to continue faithfully serving in student ministry, trusting that God uses every opportunity to impact lives for His glory.

William had been married for nine years without a child. During that time, he faced deep pain and constant mockery from people who called him names and laughed at his situation. The pressure became so heavy that he dropped out of university because the environment had grown too hostile. At one point, he even thought of giving up and committing suicide.

But God intervened. One day, during a devotional prayer at the YFC South Sudan computer center, the message touched his heart deeply. As he listened to the Word of God, he felt a great sense of relief and renewed hope, as if God was answering his prayers and reminding him to wait upon the Lord.

Later, William remarried and spent another four years still without a child. The mockery and insults continued, with people again calling him barren. Yet he held on to faith, trusting God’s timing. Today, God has surprised everyone William and his family are now expecting their firstborn child.

This journey has taught him that waiting upon the Lord is never in vain. Learning the Word of God and participating in devotions at the YFC South Sudan computer center has been life-changing. It has strengthened his faith, renewed his hope, and reminded him that God’s promises always come to pass in His perfect time.

My name is Jennifer Keji. I am a returnee from Kakuma refugee camp and a mother of six children. Life has not been easy since I came back to my own country. I am very grateful to be part of the YFC South Sudan trauma healing training. Through this program, I have found relief from some of my pain, although raising my children alone remains my greatest challenge.
I work day and night to provide food for my children after their father abandoned us. Instead of giving up or choosing suicide, I chose to fight for them by working hard. I thank the YFC ministry for giving me the opportunity to serve as a tailoring teacher. This has helped me provide for my children, and I am now able to make school uniforms for them from what we produce at the center.
I pray that God will continue to provide so that my children can go to school and make me proud as a mother. This training has helped me a lot. I now face life with courage, knowing that many people are also going through struggles like mine. I believe that one day God will see me through. My greatest joy will be to see my children going to school like any other child.

column38:
A Life changing story.
This is Justine, a 16 years old girl, grew up in a polygamous family where the mother could provide everything at home including her school fees. Life became hard and harder as she stopped schooling due to financial instability. Time came where the stepmother connived with a group of men to rape and kill Justine. She ran away from home and came to town to stay with her brother who also chased her away from his home because she could not contribute to the rent. The mother also exiled to a neighboring country since her co-wife wanted to kill her.
 At a tender age, Justine resorted to sleeping around with different men to have food and shelter and it was through this that she conceived her baby. Friends encouraged her to do abortion because she never knew the owner of the pregnancy but she refused because the pregnancy had matured. A Samaritan woman saw how vulnerable she was and referred to hospital that brought her to Youth for Christ Uganda for assistance.
At this point, Justine testifies the goodness of the Lord ever since she landed in this place. The love and care she has received, has completely turned her life around. Justine met GOD, confessed Christ Jesus as her personal Lord and Savior, sought forgiveness from GOD and from her mother, forgave all who wronged her especially her father and the step mothers. On the reunion of young mothers on 13th December 2025, she is the only one who gave her life to the Lord, we praise God for she is growing in the Lord.  She gave birth to a boy child and named him “Miracle” because God has loved her dearly. She promises to continue praying, loving her baby and making right decisions. And also going back to school if she gets the chance.
She is thankful to Youth for Christ Uganda- Mirembe House and GOD for placing such people to help vulnerable pregnant girls like her.
